definition: The warmth of the sun in winter; that particular pleasantness of sunlight felt against the skin on a cold day.
etymology: From Latin apricus, meaning exposed to the sun or sun-warmed, itself likely rooted in aperire, to open — as if the sun opens itself to you. The word surfaces in Henry Cockeram's 1623 English dictionary and then, charmingly, almost nowhere else, left to drift through the centuries like a cat looking for a patch of light.
usage: June sunlight carries none of apricity's bittersweet edge — it is expected, ordinary, taken for granted; but call up the word now and bank it, so that come February, when a shaft of pale gold falls across the kitchen floor, you will have exactly the right name for the gift of it.
